Low dawn sun raking hard from the east, long cold shadows stretching across wet grass, the air deep blue and every balloon edge-lit warm gold along one flank.
Pre-dawn indigo over the whole field, the sky so dark it reads almost black, each burner the only warm light anywhere, throwing short orange pools up into its own balloon.
High hard noon with the sun directly overhead pressing through each balloon so the brick glows translucent, the shadows pooled straight below, the air white-bright and one flame visible even now.
Late golden afternoon, warm raking side light from the southwest, the grass gone amber, every balloon shadow-striped on one flank, the burner flame bright orange against the deepening blue.
Sunset and the whole fleet lit orange down one flank, the shadowed flanks gone cool violet, the sky a gradient of deep red to indigo, one burner flame the purest warm note.
Blue hour with the sky a deep saturated indigo pressing down, each balloon lantern-lit from inside at full chroma, the grass a dark cool strip, the burner flame the one warm accent.
Full night and black sky, the only light the burners, every balloon a saturated glowing lantern, their colours richer and more committed in the dark than they ever read in daylight.
Overcast soft even light flat and directionless, every colour reading at full chroma against flat pearl-grey sky, the burner flame the single warm note in an otherwise cool field.
A storm sky of dark slate closing from the west, one shaft of low sun cutting under the cloud and picking three balloons out in blazing saturated colour against the surrounding gloom.
After rain, clean washed light, the grass a saturated deep green, the air sharp and clear, every balloon colour reading vivid and committed, one burner flame reflected in a wet mirror surface below.
Low mist burning off as the sun climbs, warm bars of light pressing through the white, the far balloons half-dissolved, the near ones rim-lit amber, the burner flame cutting sharp through the haze.

Hard clear high-altitude light with a deep cobalt sky, razor-edged shadows falling crisp across the grass, the air transparent and cold, the burner flame burning bright orange against the saturated blue.
Thin winter sun low and pale from the south, long blue shadows laid across white ground, the sky a washed pale gold at the horizon and the burner flame the warmest thing in the frame.
Dust in the air turning all the light warm ochre, the sky a hazy amber veil, every balloon reading warmer than its true colour, the burner flame a deeper orange lost inside the gold air.

Backlit straight into a low sun, the balloons reading as rims of fire, their colour glowing through the brick in deep saturated bands, the grass in warm shadow, one flame flaring pure brilliant white.
A rainbow band across the still-dark eastern half of the sky, the fleet fully sunlit in the foreground, their colours vivid and committed against the dark arc, one burner flame visible below.
Dawn, the sun just clearing the horizon and raking at a near-flat angle, the grass shadow-striped in alternating gold and cold blue, every balloon catching one blazing warm edge along its curve.

Deep pre-dawn, the field entirely dark blue, the sky still an unbroken blue-black, the burners carrying every scrap of warmth in the frame, each flame an amber point that pools soft orange up the inside of the balloon.

Noon under a bare open sky, the sun pressing hard through the brick from directly above, each balloon a glowing translucent dome of saturated colour, the shadows tight and dark, one flame bright even in full sun.
Late afternoon, the sun low and raking gold from the west, the grass amber, the east-facing flanks of every balloon in cool shadow, the burner flame warm copper against the cooling air.
Sunset, the sky burning orange at the horizon and deepening fast to violet overhead, one flank of every balloon lit flame-orange, the other flank gone deep indigo shadow, the air between them red.
Blue hour, the sky a rich committed indigo, the balloons glowing from inside at full saturation, the grass nearly black, the burner flame the sole warm accent in a field of cool light.
Full night, the sky absolute black, the burners the only source, each balloon a coloured lantern burning at full saturation, the grass sunk away into darkness, the air between them lit only by spill.
Overcast, the cloud a flat pearl-grey ceiling, the light directionless and even, every balloon colour saturated and vivid in the soft even light, the burner flame the one warm point in the grey.
A storm sky behind, dark and green-grey, a low shaft of sun from the west cutting under the cloud edge and isolating a cluster of balloons in hard brilliant colour, the rest in deep shadow.
